CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Muara Enim Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Muara Enim Regency Government. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muara Enim. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Muara Enim Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is the strengthening of human rights, enhancement of Protection efforts, quality of life, and increased participation of women in development. (4)
6. Women's Protection is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred; 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 13. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. (5)
14. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 15. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally. 20. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. (6)
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 28. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 29. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. (7)
30.

Article 21
(1) Victim assistance services, enforcement and legal aid as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Victim assistance services, enforcement and legal aid as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 82
The family in efforts to protect the rights of women has the role to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations against the rights of women in the household.

Article 15
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women may be submitted by the following reporters:
a. the victim;
b. family;
c. the community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of the protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may submit complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency in charge of the Protection of Women and Children, and officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

CHAPTER IX
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 84
(1) The Regency Government is obligated to conduct development and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
 a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
 b. technical guidance and training;
 c. provision of facilities;
 d. monitoring; and
 e. evaluation.
(3) Development as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by the department in charge of the Protection of Women and Children.
(4) The department in charge of the Protection of Women and Children is obligated to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 19
(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of violence who require a safe house include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 71
Special protection for child victims of physical and/or psychological violence as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter i is carried out through efforts: (36)
a. dissemination and socialization of statutory provisions that protect child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions.

Article 24
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting female victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:
a. female victims of acts of violence can resume their social life; and
b. female victims of acts of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER III
PROTECTION OF WOMEN
Part One
General

Article 42
(1) The Regency Government is obligated to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, child victims of abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and child victims of human trafficking; and
(3) The Regency Government, the community, the family and parents are obligated to make efforts to ensure that children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 22
(1) Victim assistance services, enforcement and legal aid are intended to provide assistance and protection to women victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
(2) Types of legal aid services include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court;
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regional Government provides legal aid to women victims of violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3) the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.
(19)

Article 75
Special Protection for child victims of maltreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter m shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, care, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance efforts.

Article 25
The Regency Government shall implement the repatriation and social reintegration of women victims of acts of violence in accordance with the laws and regulations.

(1) Every child has the right to obtain education and teaching in the context of developing their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.

Article 24
(1) Social reintegration is carried out in the context of reuniting female victims of acts of Violence with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
(2) Social reintegration is intended so that:
a. female victims of acts of violence can resume their social life; and
b. female victims of acts of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

CHAPTER IX
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 84
(1) The Regency Government is obligated to conduct development and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
 a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
 b. technical guidance and training;
 c. provision of facilities;
 d. monitoring; and
 e. evaluation.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 15
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women may be submitted by the following reporters:
a. the victim;
b. family;
c. the community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of the protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may submit complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency in charge of the Protection of Women and Children, and officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Article 59
Service efforts carried out by the Regency Government towards child victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 36 through Article 58 shall apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts towards child victims of acts of violence.

Article 42
(1) The Regency Government is obligated to provide comprehensive health services for children, so that every Child obtains optimal health status from the time they are in the womb.
(2) Comprehensive health services as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative efforts for basic health services;
b. exemption from cost burden for malnourished Children, children with disabilities, children with special needs, children infected with HIV/AIDS, child workers, child victims of abuse of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic substances and other addictive substances, children who are victims of violence, and child victims of human trafficking; and
(3) The Regency Government, the community, the family and parents are obligated to make efforts to ensure that children who are born are protected from diseases that threaten survival and/or cause disability.

Article 68
(1) Every Person is obligated to protect children from the influence of pornography and prevent children's access to information containing elements of pornography.
(2) Special Protection for children who become victims of pornography as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter f is implemented through efforts of guidance, assistance, as well as social, physical health and mental recovery.
(3) Guidance, assistance, as well as social, physical health and mental recovery as referred to in paragraph (2) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Part One
General

Paragraph 1
General

Article 19
(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of violence who require a safe house include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Paragraph 4
Social Rehabilitation

Article 75
Special Protection for child victims of maltreatment and neglect as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter m shall be carried out through supervision, prevention, care, counseling, social rehabilitation, and social assistance efforts.

b. female victims of acts of violence can have a decent life.
(3) Social reintegration as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out after victims receive social rehabilitation services.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

Article 21
(1) Victim assistance services, enforcement and legal aid as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Victim assistance services, enforcement and legal aid as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 15
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women may be submitted by the following reporters:
a. the victim;
b. family;
c. the community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of the protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may submit complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency in charge of the Protection of Women and Children, and officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Article 19
(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of violence who require a safe house include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 22
(1) Victim assistance services, enforcement and legal aid are intended to provide assistance and protection to women victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
(2) Types of legal aid services include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court;
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regional Government provides legal aid to women victims of violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3) the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.
(19)

Article 82
The family in efforts to protect the rights of women has the role to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations against the rights of women in the household.

Article 80
(1) Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Muara Enim Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Muara Enim Regency Government. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muara Enim. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Muara Enim Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is the strengthening of human rights, enhancement of Protection efforts, quality of life, and increased participation of women in development. (4)
6. Women's Protection is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred; 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 13. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. (5)
14. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 15. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally. 20. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. (6)
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 28. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 29. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. (7)
30.

Part Two
Prevention of Acts of Violence Against Women

CHAPTER IX
DEVELOPMENT AND SUPERVISION
Article 84
(1) The Regency Government is obligated to conduct development and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.
(2) Development and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
 a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
 b. technical guidance and training;
 c. provision of facilities;
 d. monitoring; and
 e. evaluation.
(3) Development as referred to in paragraph (2) is in order to realize the objectives of protection for women and children victims of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by the department in charge of the Protection of Women and Children.
(4) The department in charge of the Protection of Women and Children is obligated to report periodically to the Regent regarding the implementation of protection for women and children victims of violence.

Article 15
(1) Complaints of acts of violence against women may be submitted by the following reporters:
a. the victim;
b. family;
c. the community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of the protection of women and children.
(2) Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may submit complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and/or
c. by letter.
(3) In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, the agency in charge of the Protection of Women and Children, and officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 13, are also authorized to provide assistance in handling victims of acts of violence against women obtained through other information.
(4) Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by a Regent's Regulation.

Article 80
(1) Community participation in efforts to protect women and children:
a. participate in prevention and provide support for the development of programs to prevent violations of the rights of women and children;
b. provide information and/or report violations of the rights of women and children to the competent authorities; and
c. monitor the law enforcement process regarding cases of violations of the rights of women and children.
(2) Community participation as referred to in paragraph (1) is based on laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Article 57
In carrying out its duties, the KLA Task Force may coordinate and cooperate with PPT institutions and other institutions that provide child protection services.

Article 39
(1) Every education unit organizer must provide opportunities for children to obtain educational services without discrimination.
(2) Every education unit organizer is prohibited from expelling children from educational institutions unless there is a guarantee for the continuity of the child's education.
(3) In the event that a child victim of violence experiences school dropout, the education unit organizer must coordinate with relevant agencies.

Article 19
(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of violence who require a safe house include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 21
(1) Victim assistance services, enforcement and legal aid as referred to in Article 13 letter d constitute actions by law enforcement officials to implement laws and regulations in the context of handling cases of violence against women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Victim assistance services, enforcement and legal aid as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

Article 59
Service efforts carried out by the Regency Government towards child victims of acts of violence as referred to in Article 36 through Article 58 shall apply mutatis mutandis to service efforts towards child victims of acts of violence.

Article 71
Special protection for child victims of physical and/or psychological violence as referred to in Article 60 paragraph (1) letter i is carried out through efforts: (36)
a. dissemination and socialization of statutory provisions that protect child victims of acts of violence; and
b. monitoring, reporting, and imposition of sanctions.

b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court;

e. legal aid in the mediation process.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Muara Enim Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Muara Enim Regency Government. 3. Regent is the Regent of Muara Enim. 4. Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus within the Muara Enim Regency Government. 5. Women's Empowerment is the strengthening of human rights, enhancement of Protection efforts, quality of life, and increased participation of women in development. (4)
6. Women's Protection is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, police, prosecutors, courts, social institutions, or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will or has occurred; 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive Protection from Violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 13. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of national development program policies. (5)
14. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 15. Women Victims of Violence are women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of Violence, use of Violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of Violence against women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is services aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so they can carry out their social functions normally. 20. Law enforcement is action by officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of Violence against women and Children that is gender sensitive. (6)
22. Repatriation is an effort to return women and Child victims of Violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving Region to the Region of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 28. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 29. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. (7)
30.

(1) Employers who employ women are obligated to maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace. (2) Employers are obligated to place female workers in places that are safe for women's reproductive health.

6. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child still in the womb and not yet married. 9. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regional Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of women and Children. 10. Violence is any act that results in misery or suffering whether physical, sexual, psychological and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or unlawful deprivation of a person's freedom. 11. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in decision-making processes and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity. 12. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a Child rights-based development system through the integration of government commitments and resources, community and business world that is planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's rights. 13. (5)

Child Victims of Violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide Protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide Protection and a sense of security to victims of Violence. 25. Shelter home is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual Guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender Mainstreaming is a strategy built to integrate gender into an integral dimension of planning, formulation, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of development policies, programs, and activities in the Region. 28. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 29. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on women and men, and that the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of women and men are different. Article 19
(1) The Regency Government may provide safe houses for women victims of violence.
(2) The provision of safe house services as referred to in Article 17 paragraph (2) letter b aims to protect women victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
(3) The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
(4) The criteria for women victims of violence who require a safe house include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
(5) The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and/or
c. community leaders.
(6) Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated in a Regent Regulation.

Article 82
The family in efforts to protect the rights of women has the role to:
a. protect women from conflict and violence in the household that degrades the dignity of women;
b. provide equal opportunities to women to develop themselves in the fields of education, social, economic, political and cultural; and
c. prevent the occurrence of violations against the rights of women in the household.

Article 22
(1) Victim assistance services, enforcement and legal aid are intended to provide assistance and protection to women victims of violence and witnesses with a gender-responsive approach so that victims obtain justice and legal certainty.
(2) Types of legal aid services include:
a. legal aid in the reporting process and preparation of official examination reports;
b. legal aid in the prosecution process at the prosecutor's office;
c. legal aid in the examination process at court;
d. legal aid in the court hearing decision process until there is a final legal decision; and
e. legal aid in the mediation process.
(3) The Regional Government provides legal aid to women victims of violence based on the provisions of laws and regulations.
(4) In providing legal aid as referred to in paragraph (3) the Regional Government may cooperate with legal aid institutions, women crisis centers, advocates and/or other legal assistants who are gender sensitive.
